picks.title: A Christian's Honest Look at Death, Fear, and What Comes Next Ep 193
picks.summary:
If I'm honest with you, I don't want to die. I love this life. My wife, my kids, my work, that first cup of coffee and the sound of my rooster in the backyard. And yet I know there's a day on God's calendar with my name on it.
Death has been on my heart lately. Losing people close to me has a way of bringing it into focus, and it drove me back to my Bible with a hard question: how should a Christian actually think about death? What I found may have been the thing I had wrong my whole life.
Thanks for letting me share this one. Subscribe, and drop your question in the comments for a future show
picks.reason: A sincere Christian reflection on death and what the Bible teaches about it.

picks.title: Ep 1414 | A Child’s Tragic Death Forces This Difficult Question About God
picks.summary:
John Luke opens up about deconstructing his faith after years of hearing Christians use the Bible to defend conflicting ideas. Al and Christian wrestle with a local tragedy of a child’s unexpected death and the questions it raises about grief, justice, and God’s presence. The guys trace the rise of “my truth” back through the Enlightenment, naturalism, and the split between faith and reason, then consider whether artificial intelligence could be ushering in another massive shift in how people understand truth. 



In this episode: Psalm 139; Acts 17; Daniel 3:17-18; Jeremiah 20; Isaiah 55
picks.reason: Personal faith doubts and grief after a child's death examined honestly.

picks.title: Proverbs: Focus on the Wisdom of Women I Handmaidens, Harems, Heroines I Lynne Wilson
picks.summary: What can Proverbs and Ecclesiastes teach us about the women of the Bible—and why does recognizing their voices, wisdom, strength, and influence matter?In this episode of Women in the Old Testament, Lynne Hilton Wilson explores the books of Proverbs and Ecclesiastes, uncovering the many ways women appear throughout these fascinating books of wisdom literature. From Woman Wisdom and the warnings surrounding the “strange woman” to the powerful mother who counsels King Lemuel and the remarkable woman of valor in Proverbs 31, women are woven throughout the teachings and poetry of these ancient text
